mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows the model to assign Permitted outcome to operations where the caller's role is not allowed to perform the operation, directly violating least privilege.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DisallowedRoleOp { some op: AccessOperation | not (op.caller.role -> op.operationKind in PermMatrix.allowed) and op.auditEntry.outcome = Permitted }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows RecordsLookup operations to succeed for clinicians not on the patient's care team, violating the core ownership-based access control rule.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_UnauthorizedLookup { some op: AccessOperation | op.operationKind = RecordsLookup and op.auditEntry.outcome = Permitted and no m: CareTeamMembership | m.clinician = op.caller and m.patient = op.patient and m.status = Active }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows operations to exist with audit entries that do not correctly attribute the operation to the actual caller or patient, breaking auditability.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MisattributedAudit { some op: AccessOperation | op.auditEntry.clinician != op.caller or op.auditEntry.patient != op.patient }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows the permission matrix to be redefined with incorrect role-operation assignments, such as granting AuditOfficer access to RecordsLookup or Doctor access to AuditSearch.
Removing this fact allows clinical roles (doctor, nurse, etc.) to perform AuditSearch operations, leaking audit data to non-IG users and violating role-based authorization.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ClinicianAuditAccess { some op: AccessOperation | op.operationKind = AuditSearch and op.caller.role != AuditOfficer }
